The must-sees

9 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Museum · 1759

    British Museum

    Founded in 1753 from Hans Sloane’s collection. The Great Court and the round Reading Room sit under a glass roof added in 2000.

    Look for

    Find the Rosetta Stone: one decree written in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek, the key that unlocked Egyptian writing.

  2. 02
    Palace · 1703

    Buckingham Palace

    George III bought Buckingham House as a private home, and it became the official palace under Victoria. Royal public appearances are made from its front balcony.

    Look for

    Check the flag on the roof: the Royal Standard means the monarch is in, the Union Flag means they are not.

  3. 03
    Civic building · 1870

    Houses of Parliament

    A fire in 1834 destroyed most of the medieval palace, and Charles Barry and Augustus Pugin rebuilt it in Gothic Revival style. Big Ben is the bell; the tower is the Elizabeth Tower.

    Look for

    Look to the top of the Elizabeth Tower: a lamp there is lit whenever either House is sitting after dark.

  4. 04
    Museum · 1838

    National Gallery

    Founded in 1824 so the public could see a national collection. The building on the square opened in 1838.

    Look for

    Look down in the entrance hall: Boris Anrep’s floor mosaics show public figures of his day, Churchill among them, as virtues.

  5. 05
    Church · 1710

    St Paul’s Cathedral

    The medieval cathedral burned in the Great Fire of 1666, and Christopher Wren’s new church was completed in 1710. Its dome became a symbol of survival through the Blitz.

    Look for

    In the crypt, beside Wren’s plain tomb, a Latin inscription reads: if you seek his monument, look around.

  6. 06
    Building · 1894

    Tower Bridge

    Finished in 1894, it is a bascule bridge dressed as a Gothic castle. The high walkways were built so people could cross while the road was raised.

    Look for

    The Gothic stone of the towers is cladding over a steel frame, added so the bridge would suit the Tower beside it.

  7. 07
    Fortress · 1078

    Tower of London

    The White Tower went up in the 1070s. It has held Anne Boleyn, the princes in the Tower, and, still, the Crown Jewels.

    Look for

    Look for the ravens. Legend says the kingdom will fall if they ever leave, so at least six are kept here.

  8. 08
    Square · 1844

    Trafalgar Square

    Laid out in the 1840s to remember the Battle of Trafalgar. The fourth plinth is reserved for rotating contemporary sculpture.

    Look for

    Edwin Landseer’s four bronze lions guard the base of Nelson’s Column.

  9. 09
    Church · 1269

    Westminster Abbey

    Edward the Confessor rebuilt a Benedictine abbey here, and every monarch since 1066 has been crowned in it. Poets’ Corner fills the south transept.

    Look for

    Just inside the west door, the Grave of the Unknown Warrior is the one tomb in the floor that nobody walks on.
